header.name: Discrete Structures
header.description: This is a core course in discrete mathematics, tailored for students in the B.Tech in COMPUTER SCIENCE AND APPLIED MATHEMATICS (CSAM) program. The course is intended to give students an exposure to formal mathematical language and to train students for writing clear and rigorous mathematical proofs. This course also aims to give exposure to counting techniques of discrete objects, and basic discrete structures such as graphs and groups. In addition, it covers basic concepts in discrete probability, including an introduction to the probabilistic method.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to apply and demonstrate the use of precise mathematical language to clearly express and interpret mathematical ideas.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to construct and evaluate mathematical proofs using standard proof techniques, including direct proof, contrapositive, proof by contradiction, and mathematical induction.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to write and analyze formal proofs involving discrete structures such as graphs and combinatorial identities (e.g., binomial coefficients, factorial functions), and apply these concepts to counting problems.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Ability to explain and illustrate fundamental applications of discrete structures in computer science and mathematics through relevant examples.

lecture_topics: Methods of Proofs -- Direct Proof, Proof by Contrapositive, Proof by Induction, Proof by Contradiction.
relations on a set -- equivalence relations, partial order and various properties of different types of relations on a set
Solving Recurrence Relations including linear recurrence and divide and conquer
Graphs Theory -- basic topics that includes (but not limited to) paths, cycles, connectivity, trees, graph coloring, chromatic number, shortest path, bipartite graphs, vertex/edge-cuts
Basic Group Theory -- monoid, groups, subgroups.
